principle: TTF learns from training species without seeing the named boundary. External biogeographic boundary geometry is frozen prospectively and used only after held-out transfer scoring.
admissibility: important biogeographic boundary defined independently of the focal trait
multiple replicate species or systems when used for a cross-species TTF claim
georeferenced observations spanning the relevant spatial domain
trait measurement not selected or tuned using TTF response
species inclusion frozen before TTF outcomes are inspected
external boundary geometry frozen before final scoring
primary TTF field is fit blind to the named boundary
pairwise genetic distance matrix cells are never shuffled

benchmarks.boundary_system: Amazon Basin riverine and habitat structure
benchmarks.replicate_units: 66 bird species, 587 source samples before downstream QC
preflight_contract: download/list only metadata and coordinate-bearing small files before any VCF outcome is opened
determine per-species sample counts and coordinate coverage without using published Fst, Dxy, clustering or TTF outcomes
freeze an eligibility rule before genetic distances are computed
run semi-synthetic shared/private worlds on the retained real specimen geometry before acquiring VCFs for TTF
benchmarks.eligibility_draft: valid coordinates; species-local graph possible; minimum support chosen prospectively from geometry only; no inclusion or exclusion based on genetic differentiation
benchmarks.ttf_plan: if actual-geometry type-I and power gates pass with a sufficiently large held-out species set, acquire the 32.48 MB VCF archive and only then compute prospectively frozen genetic dissimilarities
